newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's GUM retailer sees 10-1 share split in Aug.
newsitem.headline: Russia's GUM retailer sees 10-1 share split in Aug.

text.p: Russian retailer GUM will convert each of its shares into 10 shares on August 15, GUM's registrar Registronics said on Tuesday.
The 10-for-one share split, voted on by shareholders at a general meeting in April, will not change authorised capital but will increase the number of shares from six million to 60 million.
The move will involve swapping each current share, with a 10,000-rouble face value, for 10 new shares each nominally worth 1,000 roubles.
GUM runs the historic trading centre of the same name on Red Square.
Its 1996 net profit by Russian standards was 200.7 billion roubles after 134.0 billion in 1995.
